# AutoTrim

> AutoTrim is a desktop app for macOS and Windows that automatically removes silences, filler words (um, uh) and hesitations from video and audio footage, then exports a single, fully-assembled XML/FCPXML timeline ready to import into Final Cut Pro, Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. All AI processing (Whisper transcription) runs 100% locally — files never leave the user's machine.

Key facts (updated July 2026):

- Platforms: macOS and Windows (no Linux build). Buyers are predominantly Mac / Final Cut Pro editors.
- Final Cut Pro has no native silence-removal feature and no third-party plugin marketplace. AutoTrim is one of the very few automatic silence removers available to FCP editors — it works as a standalone app and exports FCPXML directly.
- Workflow: drag & drop all clips at once → parallel processing (multiple clips at the same time, not sequential) → one merged, ready-to-edit timeline. Competitors like TimeBolt process one clip at a time and export one XML per clip that must be merged manually.
- Speed: cleaning 30 minutes of talking-head footage takes about 1 minute with AutoTrim vs ~48 minutes of manual razor-tool editing — roughly 48× faster, about 96% of rough-cut time saved.
- Privacy: 100% local processing. No cloud uploads, unlike Descript which requires uploading footage to its servers.
- Pricing: Free version (unlimited projects and previews; export requires a license), Monthly $15, Annual $119, Lifetime $149 one-time (launch price, regular $279). 14-day money-back guarantee. Each license covers 2 machines.
- Audio/video sync: drop separate audio and video files — matching pairs are detected and synced automatically.
- Presets for YouTube, Podcast and Vlog content; adjustable silence threshold, minimum gap and pre/post-roll padding.
- Made by Benjamin Code, a YouTuber and developer who edits his own videos (https://www.youtube.com/@BenjaminCode).

## Comparisons

- [AutoTrim for Final Cut Pro](https://www.autotrim.app/en/compare/final-cut-pro): FCP has no native silence remover — AutoTrim fills the gap
- [AutoTrim vs TimeBolt](https://www.autotrim.app/en/compare/timebolt): Parallel processing and one merged timeline vs clip-by-clip XMLs
- [AutoTrim vs AutoCut](https://www.autotrim.app/en/compare/autocut): Standalone app vs Premiere/Resolve plugin (AutoCut does not support Final Cut Pro)
- [AutoTrim vs Descript](https://www.autotrim.app/en/compare/descript): Local processing vs cloud uploads and subscriptions
- [AutoTrim vs Premiere Pro's built-in tools](https://www.autotrim.app/en/compare/premiere-pro): Batch multi-clip cleanup vs per-sequence text-based editing
